correctness.rationale: For all n>=2, leading kernels of corank-one products force every root arrow and at least one arc per nonroot pair. A rooted corank-one map factors e_(a->0) g with g singular on nonroot points, while unrooted corank-one maps are the corresponding unpointed singular maps. A rank-increasing splitting argument factors every lower-rank map into top-rank maps. Conversely, the preimage of 0 cannot shrink through pointed factors, so nonroot singular maps require nonroot generators. The classic strong-tournament generation criterion is cited, not assumed novel. Minimum-size cases n=2,3 are treated separately; recurrence counts source strong components. Finite checker exhausts all tournaments for n=4,5 and a strong n=6 construction; VERIFY_OK (verify.py, VERIFY_OUTPUT.txt).

value.rationale: The ambient pointed monoid arises naturally in a 2026 dominion problem. The new classification solves an exact minimal idempotent-generation problem for its singular ideal over every n, including a sharp n=3 exception, a complete necessary-and-sufficient criterion for any idempotent generating set, and the precise strong-tournament enumeration of all minimal sets. The constraint that one point be fixed creates compulsory root arrows and genuinely different generating-set geometry. The result is structural, not a numerical recomputation of the ambient monoid size.
